analyst_view.overall: Inter (17th, 6 points) and Stuttgart (15th, 7 points) both want to climb towards the top eight. Inter drew 4-4 at Atalanta on Sunday with Pio Esposito scoring a hat-trick; Calhanoglu, Zielinski and Bonny are out and all three are counted, Bastoni is back from his ban, and Italian previews expect Lautaro Martinez, short of rhythm, on the bench; one injury list today still has Thuram out with the muscle problem he picked up in mid-November and Akanji and Stankovic doubtful, so Inter's front line is not settled. Stuttgart drew 0-0 at Schalke; Jaquez and Sauer are out (counted), and Angelo Stiller was cleared to travel according to Bild, though one list today still has him out with a groin problem. French referee Francois Letexier (about 4 cards a game) is named and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals (1.9 Inter, 1.2 Stuttgart), already taking off Calhanoglu, Zielinski and Bonny. What they can't see is Lautaro likely starting on the bench and doubts over Thuram's fitness, which leaves Inter's attack leaning on Esposito; I lean a little lower, to about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, 6.2 for Inter, already lifted for Inter's recent corner run. Inter's wing-backs drive a lot of corners whoever plays up front, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, with Letexier's average record barely moving them. There is no rivalry and nothing in the news points to a rougher game, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.8 shots, 21.5 for Inter after a big lift for their recent shooting (+19.9%). Inter will shoot a lot at home with or without Lautaro, and Stuttgart's shot count depends on Stiller's fitness, which is unclear, so I stay at 32.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 on target, lifted for Inter's recent accuracy. With Lautaro likely on the bench and Thuram's fitness in doubt, Inter's finishing quality dips a little, so I trim to about 10.3.
